discussion_comments.comment_body:
Intentionally not enforcing this in the schema. The runtime degrades gracefully rather than failing: when `retain_content_in_object_storage` is set without object storage on the logs store, the logging plugin logs a one-time warning (`retain_content_in_object_storage is enabled but the log store has no object storage configured; content-disabled requests are dropped entirely`) and falls back to the default behaviour of dropping content. That is a safe no-op — content is dropped, not leaked — so turning it into a schema violation would convert an ineffective setting into a hard boot failure.

It also could not act as a real guarantee: this is a DB-backed `client` setting that the UI can toggle at runtime with no `config.json` involved (the UI already disables the switch when object storage is not connected), so schema validation only ever sees one of the two ways the flag gets set.

On the second site — the `logging` plugin config block — the built-in logging plugin is always constructed from `ClientConfig` in `server/plugins.go` and never reads user-supplied plugin config, so keys there are inert regardless.
